population: Age >=50 with spontaneous ICH, cognitive impairment, or TFNE and MRI plus tissue
setting: 10 North American and European academic centres
index_test_or_exposure: Boston v2.0 MRI-clinical criteria
reference_standard: Neuropathologic CAA assessment from biopsy, hematoma evacuation, or autopsy
outcome: Probable CAA sensitivity, specificity, and AUC
key_result: Derivation 74.8%/84.6%; temporal validation 92.5%/89.5%; geographic validation 80.2%/81.5%; full-autopsy subset 74.5%/95.0%, AUC 0.848
major_limitations: Retrospective tissue-selected sample; heterogeneous tissue extent and clinical presentations; not validated as population screening
applicability: Strongest for symptomatic referral populations resembling enrolled cases

design: prospective population-based inception cohort; model development and diagnostic accuracy
population: Adults with first-ever CT-diagnosed ICH who died and underwent research autopsy
index_test_or_exposure: CT subarachnoid extension, finger-like projections, and APOE e4
reference_standard: Masked standardized neuropathology
outcome: CAA-associated lobar ICH
key_result: Among 62 lobar ICH cases, 36 had moderate/severe CAA; three-variable model c-statistic 0.92; rule-in specificity 96%
major_limitations: Only 62 lobar ICH cases; internal bootstrap validation; genotype may not be available; restricted to lobar ICH
applicability: Applicable to acute lobar ICH evaluated by CT; not other CAA presentations

population: Three patients meeting probable CAA during life but without CAA on routine neuropathology
index_test_or_exposure: Lobar CMB location on in vivo, ex vivo 3T, and selected 7T MRI
reference_standard: Serial histopathology of targeted lesions and culprit vessels
outcome: Pathologic substrate of lobar CMBs
key_result: Seven true CMB correlates were retrieved; culprit vessels showed moderate/severe arteriolosclerosis and no CAA; lesions tended toward juxtacortical/subcortical WM
major_limitations: Extreme selected case series; only three patients and seven confirmed CMBs; localization hypothesis exploratory
applicability: Demonstrates counterexamples, not frequency or diagnostic accuracy

population: Autopsy cases with definite CAA and non-CAA controls
index_test_or_exposure: In vivo/ex vivo MRI-visible PVS and segmented histologic EPVS
reference_standard: Regional and single-vessel histopathology
outcome: Association of EPVS with vascular amyloid and vessel-wall changes
key_result: EPVS were mainly around WM portions of perforating cortical arterioles; burden associated with CAA severity in overlying cortex; affected vessels showed smooth-muscle loss and vascular amyloid
major_limitations: 19 CAA and 5 controls; selected autopsy material; cross-sectional spatial association cannot establish flow direction
applicability: Supports spatial biological plausibility; not standalone diagnostic accuracy

short_name: BBB leakage and inflammation across CAA vessel grades
population: Seven definite CAA cases: two MRI-targeted severe cases and five consecutive cases
index_test_or_exposure: CAA vessel grade
reference_standard: Immunohistochemistry for fibrin(ogen), SMA, GFAP, and CD68
outcome: Vessel-wall leakage, smooth-muscle loss, inflammation, and remodeling
key_result: Leakage and SMA loss were more frequent at mild amyloid grade than grade 0; all remodeled grade 3/4 vessels showed leakage; inflammation predominated later
major_limitations: Seven cases; many vessel observations are not independent persons; temporal order inferred from cross-sectional grades
applicability: Mechanistic hypothesis generation; not proof that leakage initiates rupture

design: prediction model development, translation, and external cohort association
population: Community-based older adults with ex vivo MRI/pathology plus separate in vivo test and cognitive cohorts
n: 119 training; 79 pathology test; 369, 72, and 244 cognitive cohorts
index_test_or_exposure: WMH, regional FA, age, and sex combined in automated ARTS score
reference_standard: Semiquantitative autopsy arteriolosclerosis for diagnostic testing
outcome: Pathology discrimination, reproducibility, and cognitive decline
key_result: Mean ex vivo AUC 0.78; in vivo test AUC 0.79 when MRI-death interval <=2.4 years; scan-rescan ICC 0.99; higher score associated with decline in selected cognitive domains
major_limitations: Small pathology samples; performance worsened with longer MRI-death interval; oldest-old cohorts; calibration and clinical thresholds not established
applicability: Candidate research biomarker; not a clinical diagnostic test

short_name: ARTS instrumental and clinical validation abstract
population: Older adults in multisite technical datasets and Rush/ARIC cognitive cohorts
index_test_or_exposure: Containerized ARTS score
reference_standard: Technical repeatability/reproducibility; cognitive trajectories rather than pathology for clinical validation
outcome: Inter-rater reliability, test-retest repeatability, inter-scanner reproducibility, and cognitive association
key_result: ICC 0.9999 inter-rater, 0.996 test-retest, 0.955 inter-scanner; baseline ARTS associated with cognitive level and decline
major_limitations: Supplement abstract rather than complete report; limited appraisal detail; cognitive association does not revalidate pathology specificity
applicability: Strong technical signal; biological and clinical utility remain separate

short_name: ARTS vascular risk and incident outcomes
population: Diverse older adults without dementia at baseline
setting: MAP, MARS, AA Core, LATC, and ROS
index_test_or_exposure: Baseline ARTS score
reference_standard: Standard cohort adjudication of MCI, dementia, stroke, and vascular risks
outcome: Incident MCI, dementia, stroke, and risk-factor associations
key_result: Higher ARTS score was associated with incident MCI, dementia, stroke, and several vascular risk factors
major_limitations: Observational associations; score includes age/sex and MRI injury features; outcome association does not prove arteriolosclerosis specificity or treatment responsiveness
applicability: Supports prognostic association in older adults, not clinical diagnosis

short_name: Arteriolosclerosis and hippocampal sclerosis of ageing
design: multi-cohort autopsy association with digital pathology subset
population: Autopsied adults age >=80 across UK-ADC, NACC, and Nun Study
index_test_or_exposure: Regional semiquantitative arteriolosclerosis and vessel morphology
reference_standard: Neuropathologic HS-ageing
outcome: Association and vessel morphology
key_result: 226 HS-ageing cases and 1792 controls; arteriolosclerosis across multiple regions associated with HS-ageing; digital subset showed thicker/larger SMA-positive arterioles
major_limitations: Autopsy selection; historical semiquantitative ratings; cross-sectional association; HS-ageing terminology predates current LATE framework
applicability: Strong association evidence; causal direction unresolved

design: ex vivo 7T MRI and histopathology spatial association
population: Twelve human postmortem medial temporal lobe samples
index_test_or_exposure: Manually labelled vessels on 100-micron ex vivo MRI
reference_standard: Semiquantitative p-tau and TDP-43 pathology
outcome: Regional vessel density and pathology
key_result: Perirhinal cortex was more vascularized than entorhinal cortex; vessel density correlated with p-tau and TDP-43; severe preclinical tau regions had higher density
major_limitations: Twelve cases; cross-sectional; manual tracing; higher density can reflect baseline anatomy, remodeling, or selection
applicability: Exploratory spatial biology, not a diagnostic biomarker

population: Digitized slides from 47 AD, CAA, and control autopsy cases
index_test_or_exposure: Six CNN models for plaques, vascular amyloid, iron/calcium, astrocytes, microglia, and fibrin
reference_standard: Three expert human raters and prior semiquantitative scores
outcome: Pixel/object detection performance and biological analyses
key_result: Validation was good to excellent for marker models and enabled continuous mixed-effects analyses
major_limitations: Training data small and staining/platform specific; human annotations are imperfect reference; external laboratory transport not established
applicability: Research quantification workflow, not autonomous diagnosis

short_name: Boston v2.0 in ROSMAP community sample
population: Deceased ROSMAP participants with in vivo 3T MRI and detailed autopsy
index_test_or_exposure: Boston v1.0, v1.5, and v2.0
reference_standard: Moderate-to-severe autopsy CAA
outcome: Diagnostic performance; 49 participants had pathology-proven CAA
key_result: Probable v2.0 sensitivity 38.8%, specificity 83.5%, PPV 57.6%, NPV 70.3%; cortical CMB count distinguished true from false positives
major_limitations: Only 134 of a much larger autopsy cohort had usable in vivo MRI; older selected sample; interval and sequence limitations
applicability: Directly relevant to community-dwelling older adults; not identical to clinical referrals

population: Community and memory-clinic participants without symptomatic ICH
setting: Mayo Clinic Study of Aging and ADRC
index_test_or_exposure: Boston v1.5 and v2.0
reference_standard: Moderate-to-severe lobar autopsy CAA
outcome: Diagnostic performance; 28 participants had pathology-proven CAA
key_result: Probable v2.0 sensitivity 28.6%, specificity 65.3%, AUC 0.47; any CAA sensitivity 75.0%, specificity 38.5%
major_limitations: Small sample and wide confidence intervals; spectrum differs from derivation population; MRI-to-autopsy interval
applicability: Highly relevant warning for asymptomatic or cognitive-only use

population: Patients with CAA and MRI markers
index_test_or_exposure: Ordinal composite of lobar CMBs, cSS, CSO-PVS, and WMH
reference_standard: Clinical diagnosis/pathology variables depending analysis
outcome: Total CAA-related SVD burden
key_result: Composite associated with clinically meaningful disease features
major_limitations: Thresholded equal-weight components; etiologic overlap; not a diagnostic criterion; detailed extraction pending
applicability: Burden description/prognosis only

population: Patients evaluated for suspected CAA-related inflammation
index_test_or_exposure: Clinicoradiologic probable/possible CAA-ri criteria
reference_standard: Biopsy or clinicoradiologic follow-up
outcome: CAA-ri diagnosis
key_result: Probable criteria showed useful sensitivity and specificity in the reported validation
major_limitations: Selected rare syndrome; incorporation and verification biases possible; full extraction pending
applicability: Specialist evaluation of subacute inflammatory presentations

short_name: Small vessel disease and medial temporal proteinopathies
population: Human medial temporal lobe autopsy cases
index_test_or_exposure: AI and manual vascular pathology measures
reference_standard: Regional AD-related and TDP-43 pathology measures
outcome: Spatial relationships among vascular and protein pathologies
key_result: Study maps coexisting vascular and protein pathology across medial temporal regions
major_limitations: Cross-sectional postmortem design; causal order cannot be determined; complete result extraction pending
applicability: Mixed-pathology mapping rather than antemortem diagnosis

population: Older adults enrolled at three MarkVCID analysis sites
index_test_or_exposure: BOLD MRI CVR during 5% carbon-dioxide inhalation
reference_standard: Concurrent MoCA and executive-function item-response score
outcome: Cross-site association with cognition
key_result: CVR was positively associated with MoCA at every site and with executive function in the combined analysis.
major_limitations: Association with cognition is not pathology validation, diagnostic accuracy, or proof of etiologic specificity; gas challenge limits scalability.
applicability: Supports a physiological VCID biomarker, not a CAA- or arteriolosclerosis-specific test.

population: Patients with minor ischemic stroke enriched for MRI SVD features
index_test_or_exposure: Baseline BOLD CVR during 6% carbon-dioxide challenge
reference_standard: One-year quantitative MRI progression and clinical outcomes
outcome: WMH/PVS progression and clinical outcomes
key_result: Lower baseline CVR in normal-appearing tissue predicted greater WMH and PVS progression after adjustment; CVR was not associated with 1-year clinical outcomes.
major_limitations: Stroke-enriched single-region cohort, one-year horizon, multiple tissue/outcome analyses, and no direct vessel-wall pathology.
applicability: Supports temporal prediction of tissue injury in SVD but not etiologic classification.

population: Probable or definite CAA-ri across 21 cohorts
index_test_or_exposure: Clinical, MRI, genetic, and CSF features
reference_standard: Probable/definite CAA-ri with variable biopsy availability
outcome: Pooled prevalence of presentation and imaging markers
key_result: Cognitive decline occurred in 70%; FLAIR white-matter lesions in 98%; lobar microbleeds in 96%; cSS in 51%; estimates for many features were heterogeneous.
major_limitations: Predominantly retrospective reports, variable definitions and biopsy verification, selection bias, and high heterogeneity.
provisional_bias: high or unclear in component evidence
applicability: Describes the recognized CAA-ri phenotype; does not by itself validate a treatment rule.

population: CAA, AD, hypertensive ICH, and healthy-control groups
index_test_or_exposure: Global and regional amyloid PET retention
reference_standard: Predominantly clinical CAA criteria; limited pathology correlation
outcome: Group differences in global and regional tracer retention
key_result: CAA showed lower global retention than AD, higher retention than hypertensive ICH/controls, and relatively higher occipital-to-global uptake than AD.
major_limitations: Most CAA cases met probable clinical criteria rather than pathology confirmation; only two tracers dominated; threshold and timing heterogeneity.
applicability: Supports regional signal as a research candidate, not a standalone diagnostic threshold.

population: CAA-ri compared with non-inflammatory sporadic CAA
index_test_or_exposure: Clinical and standardized MRI feature review
reference_standard: Clinical CAA-ri classification; pathology available only in a subset
outcome: Frequency of ARIA-E-like and hemorrhagic features
key_result: Parenchymal hyperintensity, sulcal hyperintensity, and gyral swelling were far more common in CAA-ri than non-inflammatory CAA; CAA-ri also had more numerous lobar microbleeds.
major_limitations: Retrospective referral sample, modest CAA-ri count, incorporation/circularity risk, and incomplete pathology verification.
applicability: Useful for differential recognition in specialist settings; external prospective accuracy remains needed.
